narrative.overview:
Illumia Solutions operates in a field where every competitor defaults to dark navy surfaces and neon threat-pulse graphics. This system refuses that reflex entirely. Instead it models the aesthetic grammar of a prestigious international publication — think the Financial Times or Monocle — adapted for enterprise IT procurement.

The surface is warm vellum, not clinical white. The accent is a single crimson used with the editorial discipline of a masthead — appearing on eyebrows, active states, and critical calls to action, never decorating for its own sake. Newsreader, a contemporary editorial serif with classical proportions, carries all headlines and display type; Inter handles body text and labels with the precision of a caption typeface. The system is typography-first: the grid, spacing, and components exist to serve the text, not the reverse.

This system explicitly rejects the cybersecurity dark-mode aesthetic (navy, neon, threat dashboards), the SaaS-cream template (gradient text, glassmorphism, hero metrics row), and the generic MSP checklist website. It operates in a premium register where restraint is the proof of confidence.
keyCharacteristics: Typography-first hierarchy: serif display weight dominates every opening surface
Single-accent discipline: Crimson Authority (#b31c33) used on no more than 10% of any given surface
Tactile surface depth: flat at rest, depth earned on interaction
Dual-register surfaces: warm light pages for content, obsidian footer as a distinct closing register
Motion reinforces confidence: ease-out curves, no bounce, no choreography for its own sake

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Crimson Authority appears on no more than 10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. Do not use it as a section background, as body text color, or as decorative fill.

rules.name: The Whisper Divider Rule
rules.body: Use Outline Blush (#e2bebd) for all dividers and borders. Every structural line in the system carries the brand's warmth.

rules.name: The Italic Signature Rule
rules.body: Every major headline surface contains at least one Newsreader italic phrase in Crimson Authority. Reserved for hero H1s only.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Obligation Rule
rules.body: No section or card headline appears without an eyebrow label (Inter, uppercase, tracked, Crimson Authority). No headline stands alone.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only in response to state (hover, focus, structural layering). A shadow on a resting content card is a mistake.

dos: Do use Newsreader italic in Crimson Authority for one emphasized phrase per major display headline.
Do prefix every section and card heading with an eyebrow label (Inter, uppercase, tracked, Crimson Authority).
Do use Outline Blush (#e2bebd) for all dividers, borders, and separators.
Do keep feature card grids asymmetric with the Crimson Authority card as visual anchor at grid position 0.
Do use tonal surface steps (Warm Vellum to Warm Vellum Low to Warm Vellum Container) to create section pacing without visible borders.
Do animate with fade + translate-Y at 200–700ms using ease [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] for entrances.
Do constrain body text to max 65ch line length on all description blocks.
Do use italic Newsreader for footer column headings.
donts: Don't use dark navy with neon accents (the Crowdstrike/Palo Alto aesthetic).
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient background).
Don't use glassmorphism as default. The glass-header class is limited to the navbar.
Don't deploy the hero-metric template (large number, small label, gradient accent row below CTAs).
Don't use identical card grids (same size, same icon + heading + text repeated across all positions).
Don't use border-left greater than 2px as a decorative colored stripe on resting cards or list items.
Don't use #000 or #fff for any text or background value. Every neutral is warm-tinted.
Don't produce any surface that could pass for a generic Tailwind landing page template.
